How is war/conflict conducted or resolved

This is two separate questions, so I'll explain both.

"Conducted" : Through the usage of "[CONFLICT]". One action a time, a player may initiate an action that affects the opposing player. The "[CONFLICT]" will not be resolved in favor of either user until both users have expressed awareness.

These actions must have sufficient realistic proof -enough to be accepted as reasonable by the community.

If I, roleplaying as Sealand, declared "[CONFLICT]" Sealand sends Bombers to Liberland" many players would question this. "Where did Sealand get bombers?" It would be up to me to defend the claim that my action is reasonable. This can be done by providing evidence that Sealand has those resources in real life, or by proving in game I have 1. Had sufficient resources to; 2. Acquire Bombers.

"Resolved". See /user/thehivemind's comment.

Losses will be calculated based on historical data, and reason.

Note: We are not keeping track of economic success. The main purpose of improving your Nations's resource acquisition and revenue through trade is to utilize it as reasonable evidence for future claims.

For instance: "[EVENT] Sealand Launches Moon Rocket" would have a similar issue as in my previous example. "Where did Sealand get Rockets? How did they afford them?" It would once again be up to me to provide sufficient evidence that what I am doing is reasonable. If I had begun development 6 months ago, from fund in documented trade agreements, I may be able to reasonably launch rockets. (Although, that's not sufficiently reasonable. Rockets are expensive and take a long time to build :p)

If you are conquered, you essentially lose your claim, although it is up to your Conqueror to some degree. They would be able to give you limited permissions. Feasibly, you could attempt to rebel, but once again you would need to provide evidence that it is reasonable.

If you do lose your claim, you can request another one assuming they're available.

Since then I have witnessed three reddit exoduses, each going smoothly except for the most recent one which started about six days ago or so. With such a large number of new users from the one site, we are being overwhelmed with shitposts, spam and karma whores. This place might look similar to reddit aesthetically but it in no way functions the same. These people are coming here, using Voat like it was reddit, posting the way redditors post, using reddit inside jokes, and poisoning the community. I'm all for the growth of Voat but the new people who join us have to assimilate into our community and behave like Voaters, not redditors. There have been a few new users (not going to name any names) that have constantly spammed and shitposted for the whole time they have been here, in some cases getting over the 100 CCP restriction in less than one day just because of the sheer volume of comments. I love Voat for everything that it's not. It's not reddit. But it's fast turning into it because people are unwilling to change or to learn. All they want is to be so popular on this great new site with all their imaginary internet points.

Anyway, thanks to those of you who have read my little rant, it's something that I am very passionate about and I don't want to have to look for an alternative for Voat.
